name: Okta System Log
description: Okta System Log events: who did what, from where, to which target, and how it came out. One feed for the OktaIM2:log sourcetype (Splunk_TA_okta_identity_cloud) and Okta_CL (Sentinel's Okta Single Sign-On solution).
source: Okta System Log LogEvent schema (okta-management-openapi-spec); Splunk_TA_okta_identity_cloud field extraction; the Okta SSO solution's OktaSSO.yaml parser

feed.label: Okta System Log
feed.description: Okta's System Log: one record per identity event, sign-ins, MFA, admin actions and Okta's own threat detections, with the actor, client, outcome and any target it names.

event_id.label: Event id
event_id.description: A unique identifier for one System Log event.

event_time.label: Published time
event_time.description: When the event was published to the System Log.

event_type.label: Event type
event_type.description: The published event type, for example user.session.start. Okta's own catalog names every value; it is the field to filter the System Log on.

legacy_event_type.label: Legacy event type
legacy_event_type.description: The matching Events API objectType value, kept for backward compatibility with queries written against the older API.

log_version.label: Log schema version
log_version.description: The System Log schema version the event was published under.

severity.label: Severity
severity.description: How severe Okta rates the event: DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR.

display_message.label: Display message
display_message.description: A human-readable summary of the event, the same text the Admin Console shows.

actor_id.label: Actor id
actor_id.description: The actor's own id: a user id, or an IP address string when the actor is unauthenticated.

actor_type.label: Actor type
actor_type.description: What kind of entity the actor is, for example User or IP address.

actor_alternate_id.label: Actor alternate id
actor_alternate_id.description: The actor's human-readable identifier, usually the email address that signed in.

user_agent.label: User agent
user_agent.description: The raw HTTP User-Agent string of the client that triggered the event.

client_os.label: Client OS
client_os.description: The operating system the client runs on, decoded from the user agent.

client_browser.label: Client browser
client_browser.description: The web browser the client used, decoded from the user agent.

client_zone.label: Client network zone
client_zone.description: The name of the Okta Network Zone the client's address maps to, when one matched.

client_device.label: Client device
client_device.description: The kind of device the client operates from, for example Computer.

client_id.label: Client id
client_id.description: For an OAuth request, the id of the OAuth client; for an SSWS token request, the id of the agent.

source_ip.label: Client IP address
source_ip.description: The address the client's request came from.

client_city.label: Client city
client_city.description: The city Okta's geolocation maps the client address to.

client_country.label: Client country
client_country.description: The country Okta's geolocation maps the client address to.

client_state.label: Client state or region
client_state.description: The state or region Okta's geolocation maps the client address to.

client_postal_code.label: Client postal code
client_postal_code.description: The postal code Okta's geolocation maps the client address to.

outcome_result.label: Outcome result
outcome_result.description: The result of the action: SUCCESS, FAILURE, ALLOW, DENY and the other LogOutcome values.

outcome_reason.label: Outcome reason
outcome_reason.description: Why the outcome landed where it did, for example INVALID_CREDENTIALS.

target_id.label: Target id
target_id.description: The id of the entity the actor acted on. An event can carry more than one target.

target_type.label: Target type
target_type.description: What kind of entity a target is, for example AppInstance or AuthenticatorEnrollment.

target_alternate_id.label: Target alternate id
target_alternate_id.description: The target's human-readable identifier, when it has one.

transaction_type.label: Transaction type
transaction_type.description: WEB for a request-driven transaction, JOB for an asynchronous task.

transaction_id.label: Transaction id
transaction_id.description: Ties together every event one HTTP request or job produced.

request_uri.label: Request URI
request_uri.description: The URI path the request that triggered the event was made to, from debugContext.

threat_suspected.label: Threat suspected
threat_suspected.description: Whether Okta ThreatInsight flagged the request as suspicious, from debugContext.

debug_request_id.label: Debug request id
debug_request_id.description: A request id carried in debugContext, distinct from transaction.id.

authentication_step.label: Authentication step
authentication_step.description: The zero-based step number in the authentication pipeline. Currently always 0.

session_id.label: Session id
session_id.description: A proxy for the actor's session id; every event in one sign-in session shares it.

as_number.label: Autonomous system number
as_number.description: The autonomous system number the client's address routes through.

as_org.label: Autonomous system org
as_org.description: The organisation that operates the autonomous system the client's address routes through.

isp.label: ISP
isp.description: The internet service provider Okta's IP intelligence attributes the client address to.

security_domain.label: Security context domain
security_domain.description: The domain Okta's IP intelligence attributes the client address to.

is_proxy.label: Client is a known proxy
is_proxy.description: Whether Okta's IP intelligence flags the client address as a proxy.

vendor_app.label: Vendor app
vendor_app.description: The CIM app field the TA sets for every Okta System Log event; effectively a constant naming the vendor.

tenant_domain.label: Okta tenant domain
tenant_domain.description: The CIM dest field: the org's own Okta domain, effectively constant per tenant.

OktaIM2:log.description: Okta System Log as Splunk_TA_okta_identity_cloud indexes it: the LogEvent JSON flattened to dotted field names, plus the TA's CIM aliases.
OktaIM2:log.note: actor, client, outcome and target are nested objects; target is an array (target{}.*).

Okta_CL.description: The Okta Single Sign-On solution's raw ingest table: the same LogEvent fields, flattened to underscore-joined, type-suffixed column names (_s string, _d number, _b bool, _g guid).
Okta_CL.note: The solution also ships OktaV2_CL (a CCF connector with renamed columns) and an OktaSSO() parser function that unions both onto one shape; this pack binds the raw v1 table's own columns.

ip_shared.text: A NAT gateway, VPN exit or shared proxy can put many people behind one address; a match is a lead, not a link.

ua_client_supplied.text: The client sets its own user agent string; trivially spoofed, useful for noticing change, not for attribution.

names_not_stable.text: An alternate id is usually an email address; it survives a display-name change but not an email change.
